finding.primary: The existing source-bound builder hashed only mini_entity.c even though native 0.7 moved nearly all code into local quoted .inc units. Mutating an included unit could therefore leave the recorded entry-source SHA unchanged.
finding.secondary: The native active-profile read path stored profile_sha256 but did not verify it before using profile_json. A DB mutation could silently drift runtime application/inference configuration away from its stored profile hash.

changes: recursively hash the complete repository-local quoted include closure
bind -frandom-seed to source_closure.sha256 rather than entry-unit sha only
record path, sha256 and size for every source-closure file
fail closed on include-root escape, missing local include, non-regular source, oversized source and symlinked source path segments

mini_entity_part01.inc.change: verify active profile_json against stored profile_sha256 before exposing it to status/run; mismatches fail closed

exact_blob_binding.method: git hash-object on reconstructed exact GitHub branch bytes before execution

counterhypothesis: Quoted include files are already implicitly bound because the compiler reads them. Rejected for provenance: the produced ELF depends on them, but the prior receipt source identity did not record them and its deterministic seed did not change when an include changed.
next_discriminator: Reconstruct/fetch the exact branch native source closure in an authorized isolated build surface, run build_native_bound.py v2 with repeat >=2, require all six native source files in the receipt, then execute the profile-tamper runtime falsifier before real local/API model acceptance.
